summary: All 23 requirements implemented in 9 Java files (base package sranger). One invented default and several design choices are recorded below; nothing is unimplemented. SR-DC1 holds by construction: one branch per (mode, trigger) pair.

issues.title: Sensor 'no reading' distance is 1000.0 m
issues.raw: SR-DM5 requires a 'large default value' when no IR reading is available but gives no number.
issues.fix_directive: None needed unless the specification fixes a value; change Sensor.NO_READING_DISTANCE if it does. Negative or NaN readings are also treated as 'no reading'.

issues.title: Obstacle transition requires both the obstacle event and obstacleDetected
issues.raw: SR-Beh2 triggers Moving->Turning on the obstacle event; SR-GP1 says obstacleDetected (distance <= obstacleThreshold) is the guard on that transition. Both are used: trigger Obstacle, condition obstacleDetected.
issues.fix_directive: If the guard is meant to be implied by the event only, drop '&& obstacleDetected' from the Moving block.

issues.title: Turning: autonomous Turning->Moving outranks the tick self-transition
issues.raw: The framework delivers tick every cycle; if the tick self-loop (SR-Beh7) came first, SR-Beh5 could never fire. Order: endTask, turnDurationElapsed, tick && !turnDurationElapsed.

issues.title: endTask is the highest-priority branch in Moving and Turning
issues.raw: endTask is the operator shutdown (SR-DM3); written first in each mode block as an override.

issues.title: Initial Moving entry command issued in the constructor
issues.raw: SR-FR1 issues Move(moveVel, 0) on entering Moving, including at power-up (SR-Beh1). Java issues it in the constructor; the extracted model's initial transition may not carry this action.
issues.fix_directive: None in Java; note that the model may omit the power-up Move.

issues.title: obstacleThreshold = 0.5 is rounded up to 1 in the model's constants interface
issues.raw: The constants interface rounds fractional constants up; the obstacleDetected guard compares against it, so the model uses distance() <= 1 while Java uses 0.5. distance() is an uninterpreted sensor function, so deadlock/divergence results are unaffected.
issues.fix_directive: None in Java; the Java value is exact.

issues.title: Time source is a settable Clock class read via now()
issues.raw: SR-Var1 needs 'the current time'; a Clock class (field named timer, since 'clock' is reserved) supplies it so clockResetTime becomes a RoboChart clock and turnDurationElapsed becomes since(clockResetTime) >= TURN_DURATION.
